# Marks & anatomy

The quiet, considered look is a few fixed specs plus two pieces of negative space.
The data is the only thing allowed to be loud.

## Mark specs (fixed across every chart)

| Mark | Spec |
|---|---|
| Bar / column | **<= 24px thick** (cap it - never fill the slot; let the band's leftover be air); **4px rounded data-end, square at the baseline**; grows from a single baseline |
| Line | **2px**, round join/cap |
| Marker / end-dot | **>= 8px** (r >= 4), filled with the series color |
| Area fill | the series hue at **~10% opacity** (a wash, never a saturated block) |
| Gridlines / axes | one-step-off-surface gray, **hairline (1px), solid** (never dashed), recessive |

## The two spacers (white doing the separating)

- **Surface gap.** A **2px gap** in the surface color separates touching marks - every
  segment of a stacked bar, and every adjacent (touching) bar, the same width. Keep it
  one consistent width across a stack; neighbors one step apart read distinct because of
  the gap, not a stroke drawn around them.
- **Surface ring.** Dots and end-markers carry a **2px ring in the surface color**,
  so they stay legible where they cross a line or overlap each other. The ring is part
  of the mark's hover/hit target, not just spacing - see `interaction.md` (small dots
  are easy to under-size for hover).

Never draw a border around a mark to separate it. The gap and the ring are the
mechanism; a stroke adds data-weight ink that isn't data.

## Labels & legend

A **legend is always present for two or more series** - the dependable identity
channel; never make the reader rely on color-matching alone. Direct labels then ride
the marks to *supplement* it. **A single series needs no legend box**: there is only
one color, so the chart's title or subtitle already says what is plotted. A box with
one swatch restates the title and costs space.

- **Label selectively - never a number on every point.** A value beside every dot or
  segment is chaos and goes unread. Label the endpoint, the extreme, or the one series
  the story is about; let the axis, the legend, and the tooltip/table carry the rest.
  Direct labels work *because* they are sparing - flood the chart and they stop working.
- **Direct labels before gridlines; gridlines before a second axis.**
- **A label that won't fit doesn't get clipped - measure first.** Only place a label
  *inside* a bar or stacked segment when the rendered text fits with comfortable
  padding on both sides. If it doesn't fit: for a whole bar/column, move the label
  outside the bar end (or to the tooltip if there's no room outside either); for an
  *interior* stacked segment (which has no free end),
  skip the inline label and let the legend + tooltip carry it. Either way the value
  stays in the table view, so nothing is gated. Never use `overflow: hidden` on the
  segment to "solve" it - that crops the first/last characters and is worse than no
  label. Text never overflows or is clipped by its own mark.
- Bars -> value at the tip. Columns -> value on the cap. Lines -> value at the end.
- Y-axis ticks: round to clean numbers, compact from 1,000 up (0 / 1K / 2K); they
  carry the values you didn't directly label, so keep them unless every value is labeled.
- **Text never wears the data color.** Marks - bars, lines, dots, area fills - carry
  the series color; labels, values, legends, and axis text use **text tokens**
  (primary / secondary / muted). A light categorical hue (yellow, aqua) is illegible
  as text on the surface. Identity comes from the colored mark *beside* the text - a
  dot, a short line-key, a swatch - never from coloring the text itself. A label set
  *inside* a colored fill (a stacked segment, a map tile) is the one exception: pick
  white or ink by the fill's luminance so it always clears contrast.
- **When end-labels collide, don't stack them.** Direct end-labels work when series
  separate at the right edge. When lines converge, nudging labels apart vertically
  detaches them from their lines and reads as noise - instead use **leader lines**
  (a thin connector from label to line-end), facet into **small multiples**, or fall
  back to the legend + tooltip. Past ~4 converging series, small multiples is usually right.

## Figures - when the form is a number

- **Stat tile** contract: `label` (sentence case, no trailing colon) · `value` (Sans
  semibold, auto-compact: 1,284 / 12.9K / $4.2M) · `delta` (optional; signed,
  vs a named period; color = direction × whether up is good) · `trend` (optional;
  12-point sparkline in the de-emphasis hue, current period in the accent).
- **Meter:** the fill carries severity (accent -> warning -> danger); the unfilled
  track is a **lighter step of the same ramp** (blue-on-blue, etc.) so state reads
  across the whole bar.
- **Hero figure.** The single number a dashboard leads with, >=48px, in the same
  sans as everything else (never a display or serif face - it reads as off-brand
  decoration). Exactly one per view.

"""API and pipeline checks against the processed tables and the source PDFs.

Run after `python -m bmw_feedback all`:   python -m pytest tests -q
"""

import json

import pandas as pd
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from bmw_feedback import config, decision
from bmw_feedback.api import app

P = config.PROCESSED_DIR


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def client():
    with TestClient(app) as c:
        yield c


def test_overview_matches_processed_tables(client):
    o = client.get("/api/overview").json()
    quality = json.loads((config.REPORTS_DIR / "data_quality.json").read_text())
    assert o["comments"] == quality["raw_unique_comments"]
    assert o["catalog"]["variants"] == len(pd.read_csv(P / "catalog_variants.csv"))
    assert o["catalog"]["items"] == len(pd.read_csv(P / "catalog_option_items.csv"))
    assert o["catalog"]["fitment_cells"] == len(pd.read_csv(P / "catalog_fitment.csv"))


def test_feature_verdicts_match_scorecard(client):
    api = {r["feature"]: r for r in client.get("/api/features").json()}
    card = pd.read_csv(config.REPORTS_DIR / "feature_scorecard.csv").set_index("feature")
    assert set(api) == set(card.index)
    for f, r in card.iterrows():
        assert api[f]["verdict"] == r["verdict"]
        assert api[f]["n_comments"] == r["n_comments"]
        assert abs(api[f]["complaint_index"] - r["index_negative"]) < 1e-9


def test_price_list_ground_truth(client):
    """Values read off the rendered PDF pages (G60 p.13, p.18; G70 p.4; F70 p.4)."""
    items = client.get("/api/catalog/G60/items?page_type=wheels").json()["items"]
    aero = next(i for i in items if i["sa_code"] == "3G3")
    assert aero["cells"]["520d"] == {"status": "optional", "price_eur": 1520.0, "price_condition": None}
    assert aero["cells"]["i5 eDrive40"]["price_eur"] == 300.0
    assert "i5 M60 xDrive" not in aero["cells"]
    opt = client.get("/api/catalog/G60/items?page_type=optional_equipment").json()["items"]
    vv = next(i for i in opt if i["sa_code"] == "2VV")
    assert vv["cells"]["i5 xDrive40"]["status"] == "standard"
    assert vv["cells"]["520i"]["price_eur"] == 1990.0          # cheapest: 'In Verbindung mit M Sportpaket'
    variants = {(m["model"], v["variant"]): v for m in client.get("/api/catalog").json()["models"] for v in m["variants"]}
    assert variants[("G70", "i7 M70 xDrive")]["base_price_eur"] == 182400.0
    assert variants[("F70", "116")]["base_price_eur"] == 34250.0
    assert variants[("G60", "i5 M60 xDrive")]["power_kw"] == 442.0


def test_catalog_validation_passed():
    quality = json.loads((config.REPORTS_DIR / "data_quality.json").read_text())
    v = quality["option_catalog"]
    stats = pd.read_csv(P / "catalog_page_stats.csv")
    assert v["glyphs_assigned"] == int(stats["glyphs"].sum()) == int(stats["cells"].sum())
    assert (stats["unassigned"] == 0).all()


def test_evaluate_is_traceable_and_deterministic(client):
    a = client.post("/api/evaluate", json={"idea": "climate control"}).json()
    b = client.post("/api/evaluate", json={"idea": "climate control"}).json()
    assert a["policy_hash"] == b["policy_hash"] and a["features"] == b["features"]
    sales = pd.read_csv(P / "sales.csv")
    engine = client.app.state if False else None  # noqa: F841 (engine lives in api.STATE)
    from bmw_feedback.api import STATE
    cells = STATE["engine"].cells
    for f in a["features"]:
        for c in f["cells"]:
            group = decision.SALES_GROUP[c["model"]]
            vol = sales[(sales["model_group"] == group) & (sales["market_code"] == c["market"])]["volume"].sum()
            if c["recommendation"] == "Not sold":
                assert vol == 0
                continue
            comp = c["signals"]["complaints"]
            if comp.get("level") == "market":
                row = cells.loc[(f["feature"], c["model"], c["market"])]
                assert comp["n_comments"] == row["n_comments"]
                assert comp["verdict"] == row["verdict"]
            if c["market"] == "CN":
                assert comp["score"] is None            # no Chinese comments, no borrowing by default


def test_policy_change_changes_hash_and_scores(client):
    base = client.post("/api/evaluate", json={"features": ["Vehicle, climatization"]}).json()
    alt = client.post("/api/evaluate", json={"features": ["Vehicle, climatization"],
                                             "policy": {"weights": {"complaints": 1.0, "breadth": 0, "requests": 0,
                                                                    "survey": 0}}}).json()
    assert base["policy_hash"] != alt["policy_hash"]
    assert [c["score"] for c in base["features"][0]["cells"]] != [c["score"] for c in alt["features"][0]["cells"]]


def test_unknown_idea_reports_no_direct_evidence(client):
    r = client.post("/api/evaluate", json={"idea": "vacuum for pet hair removal"}).json()
    assert r["status"] == "no_direct_evidence" and r["features"] == []
    assert r["resolution"]["matches"]           # nearest features are still listed with scores


def test_classify_with_car_uses_fitment(client):
    r = client.post("/api/classify", json={"text": "the head up display is hard to read with sunglasses",
                                           "model": "G60", "engine": "BEV"}).json()
    assert r["prediction"]["feature"][0][0] == "Head-Up Display"
    assert r["prediction"]["reranked_with_fitment"] is True
    assert r["prediction"]["feature_fitment_tiers"]["Head-Up Display"] == "optional"


def test_decision_log_round_trip(client, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(decision, "log_path", lambda: tmp_path / "decisions.jsonl")
    bad = client.post("/api/decisions", json={"pm": "A", "idea": "x", "feature": "Seats", "decision": "accept",
                                              "rationale": "", "policy_hash": "p", "data_hash": "d"})
    assert bad.status_code == 422
    ok = client.post("/api/decisions", json={"pm": "A", "idea": "x", "feature": "Seats", "decision": "override",
                                             "rationale": "Known supplier fix", "policy_hash": "p", "data_hash": "d"})
    assert ok.status_code == 200
    log = client.get("/api/decisions").json()
    assert log[0]["id"] == ok.json()["id"] and log[0]["decision"] == "override"

**Repository layout after the clean-up.** The procurement (Demandra) code was moved to the git-ignored `archive/legacy_procurement/` and is also in git history.

```
bmw_feedback/          pipeline package (python -m bmw_feedback ...)
  config.py            paths, constants, verdict thresholds
  taxonomy.py          11 domains <- 224 features; 21 reason families; survey + option-list maps
  load.py              Excel readers (feedback, CN/EU + US survey, sales)
  clean.py             text cleaning, leakage removal, label + comment tables
  scoring.py           channel-adjusted feature verdicts
  classifier.py        TF-IDF + logistic regression (feedback type / domain / feature)
  option_catalog.py    best-effort PDF option-list parser (needs pypdf)
  verdict.py           PM verdict cards (feature name or free text)
  figures.py           all charts in reports/figures/
  cli.py               build | train | figures | verdict | all
reports/               REPORT.md, figures, scorecards, metrics (tracked)
data/processed/        cleaned tables (generated, git-ignored)
models/                trained classifiers (generated, git-ignored)
```

The old pipeline's ideas carry over directly:

| Old Demandra idea | BMW equivalent |
|---|---|
| E-Class → +Manufacturer → +Feature cluster | Domain → Feature → Feature + Reason |
| Cold start: borrow from similar buyers | Small features borrow from their domain |
| Economic filter | Volume and market weighting |

---

## 7. Survey, sales and option lists

![Survey vs feedback](figures/08_survey_vs_feedback.png)

- **The US survey cross-check is weak.** 30 US survey attributes were mapped to specific feedback features by hand (`taxonomy.US_SURVEY_TO_FEATURES`). Across 54 attribute × model pairs with at least 10 comments, the survey's bottom-3-box and the feedback complaint index correlate with **Spearman rho = 0.20**.
  - Free text over-samples problems people call about, such as CarPlay and Bluetooth pairing.
  - The survey measures everyone, including silent satisfied owners.
  - Treat the two as complementary. Where they agree (G70 climate control, G70 "intuitiveness of controls" at 26% bottom-3), confidence is high.

![CN/EU survey](figures/09_survey_cn_eu.png)

- **The CN/EU survey** covers markets the free-text data does not. Its weakest attributes:
  - "Connected services" (7.3–7.4) is among the three weakest attributes in 4 of the 5 model-market columns (all but EU G70). That is consistent with connected apps being a "Bad" domain in the feedback.
  - G70 EU "Value for money" is 6.5 and G70 EU "Sportiness" 7.0.
  - Luggage capacity and loading score low for the F70, G60 and G68.

![Market representativeness](figures/10_market_representativeness.png)

- **Sales vs feedback.**
  - The G60 EU accounts for 39% of 2025 G60/G68 volume but only 2% of G60 feedback. For the G70 EU it is 31% vs 0.4%.
  - China (≈25% of G60/G68 and G70 volume) has no free-text feedback at all.
  - **G60/G70 verdicts are effectively US verdicts.** Weight by sales (`reports/market_representativeness.csv`) only with care: the G70 EU weight would be ~85×, based on 13 comments.
- **Option lists.** `option_catalog.py` extracts 220 rows (name, SA code, price, standard/optional per variant) and links 20 feedback features to them. Some examples:
  - Panorama roof: SA 402, €1,180 on the F70, €1,630 on the G60, optional on all variants.
  - Automatic doors: SA 3CD, €1,600 on the G70.
  - Heated steering wheel: SA 248, optional on F70/G60, standard on G70.

  Possible uses: "is a frequently *requested* feature only available as a costly option?" (the panorama roof is flagged *Requested*), or "does a paid option underperform its price?". PDF extraction is approximate; verify any number before quoting it.

---

## 8. Other possibilities

- **Unmet-needs radar.** Rank features by request index:
  - Leading the list: Frunk (2.5), interior mirror, panorama roof (1.9), wheels/tyres (1.7), engine sound.
  - Cluster the request texts with BERTopic to get concrete feature ideas, for example "panorama roof that opens", "pet mode for climate", "multi-contour seat buttons".
- **Competitor mentions.** Comments compare with VW, Audi, Tesla and previous BMWs (e.g. "my old 740 had a sunglass holder"). A named-entity pass yields switching reasons and benchmark gaps.
- **Owner-education vs product-fix triage.** Many Source B "Difficult to Use" notes end with the advisor explaining the feature. A classifier for "solved by explanation" separates documentation and onboarding work from engineering work. Owner's Manual is one of the most requested items.
- **Root-cause linkage for defects.** Join defect mentions with warranty or workshop data (not provided) to estimate cost per complaint.
- **Severity-weighted defect index.** Use Source C severities to weight defects; "very serious" is ≈14% of Source C problems.
- **Release tracking.** With dates, compute the complaint index per software version (iDrive 8 → 8.5, OS 9) to verify that OTA fixes work.
- **Slack or e-mail digest.** A weekly job:
  1. Re-scores features.
  2. Posts features that moved from Mixed to Leaning bad.
  3. Attaches their verdict cards.
- **Interactive dashboard.** A small Flask/Streamlit app on top of `verdict.Context`: a search box for a feature or a paste box for a comment, rendering the verdict card.

---

## 9. Caveats

- **No timestamps.** Every verdict is a single snapshot.
- **Market skew.** G60/G70 feedback is 92–97% US. F70 feedback is mostly GB and JP and comes from one channel (Source A). Cross-model comparisons are adjusted for channel but not for market.
- **Domain scores include umbrella praise** (Section 4.2). Compare components with the specific-only ranking.
- **Coarse verdict scale.** Verdicts are relative to comparable features: "Mixed" means "about as complained-about as a typical specific feature", not "fine". Thresholds are in `config.py` and should be tuned with PMs on ~20 features they know well.
- **Reason labels are noisy** (Section 3, item 1). Treat reason families as directional.
- **The option-list parser is heuristic.** It also only covers German prices.

Turns raw BMW customer feedback (F70 1 Series, G60 5 Series, G70 7 Series) into a **feature verdict for product managers**: is a feature good or bad, what kind of bad (defect or usability), why, and how confident we are.

```
$ python -m bmw_feedback verdict --feature "carplay"
## Apple CarPlay -> Leaning bad
Infotainment & HMI | confidence: medium | 79 comments
Apple CarPlay is rated 'LEANING BAD' ... 26% more complaints than for comparable features from the
same channels (complaint index 1.26, 95% CI 0.98-1.65). Complaints are usability-led, mainly:
malfunction / software fault, hard to use / confusing.
```

The full analysis is in **[reports/REPORT.md](reports/REPORT.md)**: data quality, categories, verdict method, classifier results, and the roadmap for cleaning and modelling.

---

## Pipeline

```
BMW-Data/*.xlsx, *.PDF
   │  load.py        read feedback, CN/EU + US surveys, sales volumes
   ▼
clean.py             one row per comment + one row per label; strip label leakage (Source C),
   │                 templates (Source D), advisor text (Source B); lowercase; flag label noise
   ▼
taxonomy.py          11 domains ← 224 VFC features ← 84 reasons (21 reason families)

scoring.py           channel-adjusted complaint / praise / request indices with 95% intervals,

input.content:
# BMW Product Decision Studio

Feature decisions for the BMW 1 Series (F70), 5 Series (G60) and 7 Series (G70), traced to the data in `BMW-Data/`: 10,128 customer comments, the 2025 customer studies (CN/EU and US), sales volumes 2024–2030 and the German price lists (July 2026).

A PM types a feature idea ("seat massage", "climate control", "vacuum for pet hair"). The system answers per series and market with **Prioritise / Consider / Low priority / Insufficient evidence / Not sold**. Every answer carries:
- the evidence behind it: complaint verdict, breadth, unmet requests, survey weakness, sales volume;
- a suggested move taken from the price lists: fix standard equipment, make an option standard, or introduce an item another series already lists;
- comment IDs, survey rows and PDF page references for every number.

Weights and market emphasis are an explicit, hashed policy. Two PMs using the same policy and data get the same answer, and a PM override is logged with its rationale.

```
python -m bmw_feedback serve          # http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

The full analysis is in **[reports/REPORT.md](reports/REPORT.md)**.

---

## Quick start

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
# put the hackathon files in BMW-Data/ (git-ignored)

python -m bmw_feedback all            # build + train + figures (~6 min)
cd frontend && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
python -m bmw_feedback serve          # API + web app on http://127.0.0.1:8000

python -m pytest tests -q             # API checks against the processed tables and the PDFs
```

For frontend development, run `npm run dev` in `frontend/` (port 5173). It proxies `/api` to the server on port 8000.

Command-line access works without the app:

```bash
python -m bmw_feedback verdict --feature "head-up display"
python -m bmw_feedback verdict --text "The wireless charger keeps overheating my phone"
python -m bmw_feedback verdict --list
```

## The web app

| Page | What it answers |
|---|---|
| Evaluate an idea | Which features the idea matches, then a series × market matrix. Each cell has a recommendation and an evidence panel (signals, weights, reasons, quotes, comment IDs, survey rows, price-list items). Also shows the price ladder across series, an adjustable decision policy, and a form to record the decision. |
| Feature verdicts | All 224 feedback features: channel-adjusted complaint index with 95% CI, verdict, and price-list fitment per series (■ standard, □ optional) |
| Price lists | All three PDFs parsed cell by cell: variants with base price and power, standard and optional equipment per variant with prices and page references, and technical data |
| Markets | Sales by market, how well feedback covers each market, and which customer studies exist |
| Method & audit | Scoring method, classifier metrics, what the price lists changed in the models, complaint drivers, and data-quality checks |
| Decision log | Every accepted or overridden recommendation, with policy and data hashes |

Design: the BMW corporate web system (white canvas, #262626 ink, #1c69d4 for actions only, #1a2129 dark bands, square corners, no shadows). BMW Type Next is licensed, so Barlow (SIL OFL, self-hosted) stands in for it. No BMW logo files are used.

## Pipeline

```
BMW-Data/*.xlsx, *.PDF
   │  load.py            feedback, CN/EU + US surveys, sales volumes
   │  option_catalog.py  price-list PDFs: variants, base prices, ■/□ fitment per variant, option prices,
   │                     packages, technical data; validated on every build
   ▼
clean.py                 one row per comment + one row per label; strip label leakage and templates
taxonomy.py              11 domains ← 224 features ← 84 reasons; survey and price-list link maps
scoring.py               channel-adjusted complaint / praise / request indices with 95% intervals → verdict
classifier.py            TF-IDF + logistic regression: comment → type, domain, feature
                         (+ price-list fitment re-ranker when the car is known)
risk_model.py            explainable boosting machine: what drives complaints (glass box)
decision.py              idea → features → per series × market recommendation + suggested move
api.py                   FastAPI; serves frontend/dist
```

### What the price lists feed

The PDFs are parsed from glyph and text positions, not from text order. Every build checks that:
- all 1,889 ■/□ marks on the 32 table pages land in a variant column;
- all 1,128 option prices and 23 base prices satisfy gross = net × 1.19;
- power on the price pages matches the technical data for all 23 variants.

One printed anomaly (F70 p.17) is kept as printed. 106 feedback features are linked to price-list items through a curated keyword map, and each link shows the keyword that produced it.

| Layer | Use of the price lists | Measured effect |
|---|---|---|
| Feature classifier | Re-ranks candidates by the feature's fitment on the comment's car | +0.6 pp top-1 on comments about linked features (26 fixed, 4 broken, McNemar p = 0.0001) |
| Complaint model | Fitment tier, option price and % of base price as inputs | No held-out gain (AUC −0.0008, feature-grouped CV), so the production model uses context only; the price-list variant is kept for audit |
| Decision engine | Price ladder across series, standard vs optional vs not listed, suggested move | Deterministic, with page references |

## Outputs

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `reports/REPORT.md` | Findings, method, roadmap |
| `reports/model_ablation.json` | Price-list ablations for both models, EBM shape functions |
| `reports/classifier_metrics.json`, `data_quality.json` | Classifier CV metrics, cleaning and PDF-validation counts |
| `data/processed/catalog_*.csv` | Parsed price lists: variants, items, fitment, packages, technical data, feature links |
| `data/decisions.jsonl` | Decision log written by the app (git-ignored) |

## Repository layout

```
bmw_feedback/     pipeline package and API
frontend/         React + Vite web app (built into frontend/dist)
tests/            API and pipeline checks
reports/          report, figures, scorecards, metrics
BMW-Data/         raw hackathon data (not committed)
```

This repository previously held **Demandra**, our procurement demand-prediction solution for Challenge 2 of the Unite x TUM.ai Hackathon (1st place). The original code is in git history.

content.text:
## Were the PDFs factored in? No, they weren't, and now they are.

The old parser read text only. It pulled 220 rows with junk entries, linked 20 features, and fed nothing into the classifiers or verdicts. On this machine it was silently skipped because `pypdf` wasn't installed.

The new parser in [option_catalog.py](bmw_feedback/option_catalog.py) reads all three PDFs by position. It extracts:
- 23 variants with base price and power;
- 364 equipment items with per-variant standard/optional marks and prices, including rows priced differently by variant (3G3 costs €1,520 on ICE and €300 on i5/PHEV);
- 97 package entries and 555 technical values.

Every build checks the result:
- all 1,889 ■/□ marks land in a variant column;
- 1,128 option prices and 23 base prices satisfy gross = net × 1.19;
- power matches between the price pages and the technical pages for all 23 variants.

One price is misprinted in the PDF itself (F70 p.17) and is kept as printed. 106 feedback features are now linked to price-list items.

## What the PDF data changed in the models

| Model | Result |
|---|---|
| Feature classifier | Small but real gain: +0.6 pp top-1 on comments about linked features (26 fixed, 4 broken, McNemar p = 0.0001). Used when a comment is classified for a known car. |
| Complaint model (EBM, a glass-box model) | **No gain** (AUC 0.793 → 0.792). An early +0.033 came from umbrella labels like "Exterior design" (mostly praise, no price-list item), not from fitment. Production uses the context-only model; the PDF version is kept for audit. |
| Price sensitivity | Can't be tested yet: only 5 labels say "not standard / too costly". |

So the PDFs mainly drive the decision layer. That layer is a price ladder across the three series (e.g. the head-up display is €3,800 via the Innovationspaket on the 1 Series, €2,400 on the 5 Series, standard on the 7 Series). It also suggests a move per series: fix, make standard, or introduce.

## The app

`python -m bmw_feedback serve` runs the FastAPI backend and the React frontend at **http://127.0.0.1:8000**. A PM types an idea and gets a series × market grid of *Prioritise / Consider / Low priority / Insufficient evidence / Not sold*. Each cell shows the evidence behind it: signal scores and weights, reasons, quotes with comment IDs, survey ranks, sales, and price-list items with page references.

PMs can adjust a decision policy whose hash appears on every result, and can record follow/override decisions with a rationale. Other pages cover feature verdicts, the parsed price lists, markets, method and audit, and the decision log. Tests pass (9 of 9), the full pipeline ran clean, and I checked every page in a browser with no console errors.

## What to know

- **Policy defaults, not data:** the signal weights (complaints 0.4, others 0.2), the thresholds and the verdict→points mapping are my defaults. They're shown and hashed on every result, and PMs can adjust everything except the points mapping.
- **Data limits:**
  - Prices are German only.
  - The 7 Series equipment tables cover 4 of its 7 variants; the rest show as unknown.
  - There are no Chinese customer comments, so China cells say "insufficient evidence" unless the PM opts into borrowing other markets' verdicts.
  - Competitor specs and reviews aren't in the repo, so they aren't used.
- **Design:** the tokens come from [VoltAgent's BMW DESIGN.md](https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-design-md/blob/main/design-md/bmw/DESIGN.md), a third-party reconstruction of bmw.com, not official BMW documentation. Other references I checked: [shadcn BMW](https://www.shadcn.io/design/bmw), [open-design BMW M](https://open-design.ai/plugins/design-system-bmw-m/), [designmd.co](https://www.designmd.co/d/bmw). BMW's typeface (BMW Type Next) is licensed, so I used Barlow, a free substitute, and no BMW logo files. I kept the app local rather than publishing it, since it carries BMW branding.
- **Server:** it runs as a background task in this session and stops when the session ends. To restart: `cd frontend && npm run build && cd .. && python -m bmw_feedback serve`.
- **Git:** everything is uncommitted for your review.

Full write-up is in [reports/REPORT.md](reports/REPORT.md) §7, with commands in [README.md](README.md).
